messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran a replay of the longitudinal longctx workload on staging and hit repeated KV residency oscillations for tenant-A when 3+ longctx requests overlap. Behavior: residency spikes, fast evictions, then sudden reuse failures causing memory growth over ~5m. Posting logs and quick numbers below.

mira: can you paste the eviction + residency log lines? trying to understand if this is scanner policy or compaction lag.

alex: here are the relevant lines from kv-evict.log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-01T08:31:12Z] tenant=A residency=0.42 pages=1024 mark=312 evict_scan_ms=8
[2026-03-01T08:31:13Z] tenant=A residency=0.63 pages=1536 mark=1104 evict_scan_ms=9
[2026-03-01T08:31:14Z] tenant=A residency=0.21 pages=768 mark=160 evict_scan_ms=7
[2026-03-01T08:31:15Z] tenant=A mark->free_ms=120 compaction_queue_len=14
[2026-03-01T08:31:16Z] tenant=B residency=0.05 pages=80
```
Observations: mark spikes then within ~2s many pages are reaccessed and compaction lags (~120ms mark->free). That delay correlates with reuse failures and transient memory bump.

jon: my quick read: looks like an eviction race + granularity problem. Scanner marks at a coarse granularity and compaction/async free can't keep up; meanwhile longctx reaccesses reset age, so those "stubborn" pages stick around. Also fragmentation increases because we free large chunks, not smaller blocks, so reuse for interleaved tenants suffers.

sam: agree. Two levers we tried before: reduce eviction grain (64KB -> 16KB) and add per-tenant eviction watermarks with staggered windows to avoid synchronized eviction storms. Trade-offs: smaller grain reduces fragmentation but increases CPU and metadata ops.

alex: quick microbenchmark numbers:
- baseline (64KB grain, no per-tenant cap): tail latency 99p = 340ms, memory delta over 5m +22% for tenant-A under 3x longctx overlap.
- 16KB grain: tail latency 99p = 385ms (+13% CPU), memory delta +8%.
- 16KB + tenant-cap @40% residency: tail = 390ms, memory delta +2%, but token CPU cost for small requests up ~6%.

mira: those are useful. Can you also share the profiler stack for the compaction path? suspecting async free scheduling bottleneck.

alex: paste from perf flame (trimmed):
```
KV::mark_pages -> scheduler::enqueue_compact -> compact_worker::process (80% time in free_pages())
free_pages() => kmalloc/free + vm_unmap (heavy syscall pressure when many pages freed at once)
```
So bulk frees cause VM churn.

jon: idea: add a paced free path (throttle frees over 50ms window) + opportunistic coalescing on low load. That should reduce VM churn and avoid spikes in compaction queue. Also consider keeping a small per-tenant hot-pool (MRU) pinned when longctx detected so reaccess doesn't reset page age metric incorrectly.

sam: another angle: eviction policy heuristic that takes "recent-reaccess-count" into account — if a page is reaccessed >N times in T window, treat as hot despite age. That avoids chasing pages that bounce between tokens in the same longctx.

alex: I reproduced the reaccess-reset bug: when page touched inside same sequence we reset age_metric to 0 which prevents it from being chosen for compaction. A patch to only bump age if touched by a different request reduces the oscillation in my small replay.

mira: nice find. That could be a quick win. Any perf downside?

alex: minimal — it just distinguishes reuses from cross-tenant touches. But we need to be careful with multi-worker reaccess semantics.

infra-bot: @channel deploy 2026-03-01T09:12 completed on staging (kv-cache: feature/eviction-traces)

sam: suggested action items: 1) run a 24h noisy-neighbor sim with (16KB grain + per-tenant watermarks + paced free), 2) add counters: mark->free latency histogram, compaction_queue_len per-tenant, reaccess-reset count, 3) experiment default cap in {30%,40%,50%} and collect cost/latency tradeoffs.

mira: I'll book a 30m sync tomorrow to triage results and add to perf board. I'll also create a small reproducer that toggles the reaccess-reset flag so we can A/B it on staging. :thumbsup:

jon: one more note — when running sim, include a small fraction of bursty small requests (1-5 tokens) interleaved with longctx to catch worst-case fragmentation for small tail latency.

alex: repro command I used: `runtest --replay tenants_longctx.json --workers 32 --duration 10m --trace eviction`

mira: thanks — leaving this here. We'll sync tomorrow and decide on the default heuristic.
